title: Longest Palindrome After Substring Concatenation I
statement:
Cut one contiguous piece (a substring) out of the string `s` and another out of the string `t`; either piece is allowed to be empty. Writing the piece from `s` and then the piece from `t` produces a new string.

Return the greatest length such a string can have while being a palindrome, meaning it is identical to its own reverse.
constraints: s and t contain only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Both strings have at most 30 letters, so each has at most 465 non-empty substrings. Pairing every piece of `s` with every piece of `t` (the empty piece included) gives fewer than 250,000 candidates, and a two-pointer palindrome test on each one is cheap. With limits this small, plain enumeration is the whole solution; the faster dynamic-programming idea is only needed when the strings grow to 1000 letters (problem 3504).

## Approach

1. `isPalindrome(text)` moves `left` and `right` toward each other and fails at the first pair of different letters.
2. Choose the piece of `s` by its start `sStart` and end `sEnd` (exclusive); `sStart === sEnd` is the empty piece. Call it `front`.
3. Choose the piece of `t` the same way with `tStart` and `tEnd`, and append it to `front` to get `candidate`.
4. Only a `candidate` longer than `best` can improve the answer, so only those are tested; a palindrome among them becomes the new `best`.
5. After every pair has been tried, return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "a"`, `t = "a"`. First `front` is empty (`sStart = 0, sEnd = 0`). Joined with the `t` piece `"a"` it gives `candidate = "a"`, longer than `best = 0` and a palindrome, so `best = 1`. Next `front = "a"` (`sEnd = 1`): with the empty `t` piece the candidate `"a"` is not longer than 1 and is skipped, but with the `t` piece `"a"` the candidate `"aa"` is a palindrome of length 2, so `best = 2`. No later candidate is longer than 2, and the answer is 2.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n²·m²·(n + m)) for `n = s.length` and `m = t.length`: about n²/2 pieces of `s` times m²/2 pieces of `t`, each joined and tested in O(n + m).
- Space: O(n + m) for the candidate string.

## Pitfalls

- Either piece may be empty: in Example 3 the best answer `"aaaa"` takes nothing from `s`.
- The piece of `s` always comes first. `s = "ab", t = "a"` makes `"aba"` (3), but `s = "a", t = "ab"` only reaches `"aa"` (2).
- Pieces are contiguous: from `s = "abc"` you cannot take `"ac"`.
- The test `candidate.length > best` only skips work; drop it and the answer stays the same, just slower.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | length of the longest palindrome found so far |
| `sStart`, `sEnd` | start and end (exclusive) of the piece of `s` |
| `front` | the piece `s.slice(sStart, sEnd)` |
| `tStart`, `tEnd` | start and end (exclusive) of the piece of `t` |
| `candidate` | `front` followed by the piece of `t` |
| `left`, `right` | the two pointers inside `isPalindrome` |
